title: Care Navigator/Receptionist
description: Due to a member of the team upskilling into a new role, we are seeking a Care Navigator/Receptionist to join our fast-paced reception and administration team. We are looking for individuals who feel they will be able to settle into a busy practice, whilst able to work independently and as part of a team. Previous primary care or GP surgery experience is desirable, although applicants with relevant transferable skills will also be considered. Provide a professional and welcoming first point of contact for patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. Manage a busy telephone system, responding to enquiries and directing patients to the most appropriate service. Book, amend and cancel patient appointments in accordance with practice protocols. Receive patients at the reception desk, recording arrivals and assisting with enquiries. Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures. Deal with incoming emails, post and other administrative correspondence. Liaise effectively with GPs, nurses, pharmacists, hospitals and other healthcare organisations. Carry out administrative tasks relating to patient records, including scanning, document management and filing. Follow practice protocols to ensure consistent and high-quality care is provided to our patients. Act as directed by other members of the practice team. Provide reception and administrative cover for colleagues during periods of annual leave or sickness absence. Work across both Ireland Wood and Horsforth practice sites when required. Ensure confidentiality is always maintained in accordance with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and practice policies. The Care Navigator/Receptionist is an essential member of the practice team, providing a professional, efficient and patient-focused reception and administrative service across both practice sites. Working closely with the Practice Manager, GP Partners and the wider clinical and administrative teams, the post-holder will help ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the practice while delivering excellent customer service to patients and visitors. A key part of the role is supporting patients with their queries and appointment requests, helping them to access the most appropriate healthcare professional or service in line with practice protocols. The post-holder will manage appointments, respond to telephone and face-to-face enquiries, process repeat prescription requests and undertake a range of administrative duties to support the delivery of safe and effective patient care. The role also includes maintaining accurate patient records, processing correspondence and supporting communication with hospitals, pharmacies and other healthcare organisations. The post-holder will work in accordance with practice policies, maintain confidentiality at all times, and provide cover for colleagues and across both practice sites when required. Overall, this is a varied and rewarding role that requires excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, together with the ability to work calmly and effectively in a busy environment while providing a high standard of patient care and customer service.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Stanley Health Centre is looking for an enthusiastic, flexible and reliable receptionist to join our Reception team. Successful candidates will need to be able to demonstrate previous administrative and customer service experience and have the skills to adapt to and prioritise the duties of a busy reception desk, remaining calm and focused to ensure a high standard of care is delivered to patients. The ideal candidate will be a team player with excellent verbal and written communication skills. Computer skills are essential, and experience with a clinical system would be advantageous, but training will be provided for the right candidate. The post holder will also need to be flexible in their hours to cover either mornings or afternoons when required, working part-time 25 hours per week either 8am to 1pm or 1.30pm 6.30pm Monday to Friday. Stanley Health Centre Receptionist job description Job Title: Medical Receptionist Line Manager: Assistant Practice Manager Accountable to: Practice Manager Hours per week: 25 To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of information and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. Mission Statement We will strive to: Provide a service which puts patients needs and welfare at the heart of everything we do. Generic Responsibilities All staff at Stanley Health Centre have a duty to conform to the following: Equality, Diversity & Inclusion A good attitude and positive action towards ED&I creates and environment where all individuals are able to achieve their full potential. Creating such an environment is important for three reasons: it improves operational effectiveness, it is morally the right thing to do, and it is required by law. Patients and their families have the right to be treated fairly and be routinely involved in decisions about their treatment and care. They can expect to be treated with dignity and respect and will not be discriminated against on any grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Patients have a responsibility to treat other patients and our staff with dignity and respect. Staff have the right to be treated fairly in recruitment and career progression. Staff can expect to work in an environment where diversity is valued and equality of opportunity is promoted. Staff will not be discriminated against on any grounds including age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Staff have a responsibility to ensure that you treat our patients and their colleagues with dignity and respect. Safety, Health, Environment and Fire (SHEF) This practice is committed to supporting and promoting opportunities to for staff to maintain their health, well-being and safety. You have a duty to take reasonable care of health and safety at work for you, your team and others, and to cooperate with employers to ensure compliance with health and safety requirements. All personnel are to comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, Environmental Protection Act 1990, Environment Act 1995, Fire Precautions (workplace) Regulations 1999 and other statutory legislation. Confidentiality This practice is committed to maintaining an outstanding confidential service. Patients entrust and permit us to collect and retain sensitive information relating to their health and other matters, pertaining to their care. They do so in confidence and have a right to expect all staff will respect their privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. It is essential that if, the legal requirements are to be met and the trust of our patients is to be retained that all staff protect patient information and provide a confidential service. Quality & Continuous Improvement (CI) To preserve and improve the quality of our output, all personnel are required to think not only of what they do, but how they achieve it. By continually re-examining our processes, we will be able to develop and improve the overall effectiveness of the way we work. The responsibility for this rests with everyone working within the practice to look for opportunities to improve quality and share good practice. This practice continually strives to improve work processes which deliver health care with improved results across all areas of our service provision. We promote a culture of continuous improvement, where everyone counts and staff are permitted to make suggestions and contributions to improve our service delivery and enhance patient care. Induction Training On arrival at the practice all personnel are to complete a practice induction programme; this is managed by the Deputy Practice Manager. Learning and Development The effective use of training and development is fundamental in ensuring that all staff are equipped with the appropriate skills, knowledge, attitude and competences to perform their role. All staff will be required to partake and complete mandatory training as directed by the training coordinator, as well as participating in the practice training programme. Staff will also be permitted (subject to approval) to undertake external training courses which will enhance their knowledge and skills, progress their career and ultimately, enable them to improve processes and service delivery. Collaborative Working All staff are to recognise the significance of collaborative working. Teamwork is essential in multidisciplinary environments. Effective communication is essential and all staff must ensure they communicate in a manner which enables the sharing of information in an appropriate manner. Service Delivery Staff at Stanley Health Centre must adhere to the information contained with practice policies and regional directives, ensuring protocols are adhered to at all times. Staff will be given detailed information during the induction process regarding policy and procedure. Security The security of the practice is the responsibility of all personnel. Staff must ensure they remain vigilant at all times and report any suspicious activity immediately to their line manager. Under no circumstances are staff to share the codes for the door locks to anyone and are to ensure that restricted areas remain effectively secured. Professional Conduct Practice staff are required to dress appropriately for their role. Administrative staff will be provided with a uniform whilst clinical staff must dress in accordance with their role. Leave All personnel are entitled to take leave. Line managers are to ensure all of their staff are afforded the opportunity to take their allocated amount of annual leave each year, and should be encouraged to take all of their leave entitlement.

title: Medical Administrator
description: Previous applicants need not apply. Oakwood Lane Medical Practice is delighted to offer an opportunity for a dedicated Medical Administrator to join our friendly, forward thinking team. We care for a diverse population of over 14,000 patients and pride ourselves on delivering high quality, patient centred healthcare. We are looking for an enthusiastic, organised and proactive administrator who is passionate about supporting excellent patient care. You will play a key role in ensuring patients receive the right care at the right time, contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the practice. Join us and become part of a supportive, inclusive and dynamic team committed to delivering outstanding healthcare. Part-t ime role 24-28 hours per week. Must be able to work a Thursday. Document and Record Management Process, scan and code incoming clinical correspondence. Assign documents to the correct clinician or administrative team promptly and accurately. Identify and escalate urgent or clinically significant information. Liaise with clinicians to clarify documentation queries and ensure appropriate action. Maintain accurate patient records using workflow systems. Process incoming and outgoing patient records. Referral Administration Complete and submit patient referrals to specialists and external providers, ensuring all documentation is accurate and complete. Take ownership of referrals from initiation to completion, including monitoring rejections and responses. Provide clear information to patients regarding referral pathways and progress. Ensure all referral communications are documented and filed appropriately. Insurance and Third Party Requests Manage insurance forms, medical reports and third party documentation with accuracy and compliance. Support patients and staff with queries relating to access to medical records and permissions. General Administrative Support Provide flexible administrative cover across departments as required. Support statutory and contractual practice obligations. Assist with ad-hoc administrative tasks to ensure smooth day to day operations. Work collaboratively with colleagues and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives. Process, scan and code incoming clinical correspondence including hospital letters, discharge summaries, ambulance notifications and out of hours reports. Review correspondence and ensure documents are attached to the correct patient record. Code or free text clinical information on to the patient record. Assign documents to the appropriate clinician or administrative team promptly and accurately. Identify urgent, abnormal or clinically significant information and escalate in accordance with practice procedures. Liaise with clinical staff to clarify documentation queries and ensure appropriate actions are completed. Maintain accurate patient records using practice workflow and clinical systems. Process incoming and outgoing patient records in accordance with NHS and practice procedures, ensuring records are transferred, received and managed accurately and securely. Monitor workflow queues to ensure correspondence is processed within agreed timescales. Deal with queries relating to correspondence management and document processing. Complete and submit referrals to secondary care, community services and external providers, ensuring all supporting documentation is accurate and complete. Take ownership of referrals from initiation through to completion. Monitor referral progress, including rejected referrals, requests for further information and provider responses. Liaise with clinicians to obtain information required to support referrals. Provide patients with information regarding referral pathways, appointments and progress where appropriate. Ensure all referral activity, communications and outcomes are accurately documented and filed within the patient record. Support the practice in achieving referral processing targets and standards. Manage insurance reports, medical reports and third-party documentation requests in accordance with practice procedures and relevant legislation. Ensure documentation is completed accurately and within agreed timescales. Support patients and staff with queries relating to access to medical records, consent and permissions. Maintain accurate records of requests, actions and outcomes. Escalate complex or sensitive requests to the appropriate manager or clinician. Statutory and Contractual Support Support the management of requests for information, reports and returns relating to the practice's statutory and contractual obligations. Assist with administrative processes required to support regulatory, contractual and operational requirements. Undertake any other reasonable duties requested by the management team in support of the practice's business operations.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking to appoint a receptionist to join our busy GP practice based over two sites, who will be the first point of contact for patients and visitors as well as carrying out general office management tasks. You will be responsible for the general reception duties within the Practice and work with our established processes, policies and procedures to provide a comprehensive high quality service and deal efficiently and courteously with patient enquiries. You will receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. You will provide general assistance to the practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. You will have excellent communication skills, a compassionate and friendly nature who can operate in a busy environment working with a range of people. This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised and an effective communicator who can provide a professional and warm welcome to our patients, ensuring every contact is of the highest quality. To have a thorough knowledge of all practice procedures. Computer data entry, processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures. Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required, including word/data processing, electronic filing, photocopying, and scanning. Cover sickness/annual leave and work reasonable overtime when required. Receiving patients, consulting with members of the practice team. Processing prescription requests from patients, dealing with prescriptions queries from patients and pharmacies. Be able to cover all reception positions as necessary. Taking messages and passing on information. Processing personal and telephone requests for appointments, telephone consultations and home visits and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional. Processing and distributing incoming (and outgoing) mail. Ensure that system is operational at the beginning of each day and switched over to night service and that the answer phone is operational at the end of each day. Keeping the reception area and notice boards tidy and free from obstructions and ensuring patient information and leaflets are well stocked. Maintaining and monitoring the practice and extended access appointments system including booking/amending and cancelling appointments, ensuring sufficient and accurate information is recorded. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare agencies and providers. Filing and retrieving paperwork. Scanning clinical correspondence onto SystmOne. APPOINTMENT SYSTEM MANAGEMENT Monitor effectiveness of the system and report any problems or variations required. CONSULTATION ROOM PREPARATIONS Consulting rooms checked, prepared and re-stocked daily in readiness for each consulting session in accordance with Practice guidelines. Ensuring the practice is left tidy and secure and rooms are checked and re-stocked in line with Practice guidelines at the end of each day.

title: Care Navigator / Receptionist
description: An exciting opportunity has arisen for a Care Navigator / Receptionist to join our busy team, working at both our Lofthouse Site and The Manse, our Rothwell Site. Care Navigators are the first line of contact with our patients and visitors. This is a varied role that includes face to face and telephone contact with patients as well as administrative duties. Reception experience/customer service is desirable, but training will be given to the successful candidate. To receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional, in a courteous, efficient, and effective way. Provide general assistance to the Practice team and project a positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Act as a Care Navigator, signposting patients to appropriate NHS services or appropriate Health Professional to meet their needs.
